label: Pet simulator / collection — pet inventory grids, rarity borders, egg-hatching screens, index books, equip slots
provenance: Researched on the open web on 2026-09-20 with WebSearch and WebFetch. Every row below names a page that was actually fetched and read in that session, except the one row that says in its own source field that it was NOT fetched. No image, no Luau source and no asset from any of these is stored or reproduced; what is recorded is the construction convention read out of what the page describes — layout, order, state, geometry, timing.

references.source: https://tryhardguides.com/how-to-equip-your-best-pets-in-pet-simulator-99/ — fetched 2026-09-20; a walkthrough of Pet Simulator 99's pets menu as it ships
demonstrates: the pets menu is opened from a button on the BOTTOM edge of the HUD, not from a side rail — the pet screen is the game's primary screen and gets the primary slot
the open menu carries exactly three controls along its TOP: a padlock, a pet face, and a four-windows icon — lock, auto-select, and grid density
equipping is AUTOMATIC by default; tapping a pet raises a prompt offering 'Edit Mode', and manual selection only exists inside that mode
the pet-face icon is the way back OUT of manual mode to automatic — the manual/auto switch is a persistent toggle in the toolbar, not a one-shot action
the equip capacity is a number the player owns (the guide works an eight-slot example), so the screen must render a capacity it is told, not a fixed row

references.source: WebSearch result text for 'Pet Simulator 99 inventory UI equip slots rarity' (2026-09-20), summarising pet-simulator.fandom.com Ranks and petsimulator99.wiki pages. FLAGGED: the Fandom and wiki pages themselves returned HTTP 402/403 to the fetcher and were NOT read. Treat this row as weaker than the fetched rows.
demonstrates: the redesigned inventory sorts pets greatest-to-lowest by strength and auto-equips the top eight
additional equip slots are unlocked by rank progression, so the slot strip grows over a player's lifetime
variants (Golden 1.5x, Rainbow 3x, Shiny 5x) are a SECOND axis on top of rarity — a tile has to show both a rarity and a variant without them fighting

references.source: https://www.thegamer.com/roblox-bubble-gum-simulator-infinity-pet-guide/ — fetched 2026-09-20; guide to Bubble Gum Simulator INFINITY's pet system
demonstrates: the equip strip starts at FOUR slots and tops out at ELEVEN — a small opening row that roughly triples, never a grid
extra slots arrive from three different sources (mastery levels, quests, a gamepass), so the strip has to render partially-filled and locked states side by side
the pet screens are reached as TABS ('Quests tab', 'Mastery menu') off one menu rather than as separate windows

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/ui-inventory-look/3580465 — fetched 2026-09-20; Creations Feedback thread, an inventory explicitly built after Pet Simulator 99
demonstrates: the assembly is: side navigation rail, header with an X at its right, and a ScrollingFrame of square slots in fixed columns
each slot carries the unit image, a level/amount badge and a rarity mark — three pieces of information on one square, no more

UIStroke is the framing device on every element, and the top critique was that 'the UIStroke color is different between the X button and the frame' — one stroke colour across frame, close button and tile or the screen falls apart
second critique: 'the content cant fully fit in the scrolling frame horizontally. adjust your cell size to make it fit!' — the grid cell is derived from the container width, never a fixed pixel size
third critique: the 'Lvl 1' / 'Lvl 50' badges drifted left because the label was not centre-anchored inside its badge
the thread's praise was for keeping 'that classic simulator feel' while staying clean — the genre's chunky construction is the goal, not something to modernise away

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-would-you-display-pets-in-a-simulator-inventory/562549 — fetched 2026-09-20; Game Design Support thread on how to display pets in a simulator inventory
demonstrates: ViewportFrame is the WRONG renderer for an inventory tile: it 'do[es] not support particles' and 'can cause lag if too many of them are used with models specially with a lot of parts'
the shipped answer is a flat pre-rendered ImageLabel per pet, produced offline against a greenscreen and keyed out
consequence for layout: a tile is an image slot of a known aspect, so the grid can be packed tightly and scrolled without a per-tile render budget

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-render-out-pets-for-a-pet-inventory-like-arm-wrestle-simulator/2668167 — fetched 2026-09-20; Art Design Support thread about matching Arm Wrestle Simulator's pet icons
demonstrates: the polished look 'looks much more like an image than a viewport frame' — a fixed camera angle and fixed lighting per pet is what reads as finished
the pet art carries its own stroke/outline baked into the render, so the icon stays readable on any tile tint
tiles are produced by cloning one template UI element into a scrolling container and filling it from data — the template is the unit of design, not the screen

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/pet-hatching-framework-part-1/1480291 — fetched 2026-09-20; Community Tutorial building an egg/hatch framework
demonstrates: walking up to an egg opens a PurchaseMenu anchored to the egg via worldToScreenPoint and SCALED by camera distance — it is a screen-space panel tracking a world object, not a BillboardGui and not a centred modal
the panel is three stacked bands: NameBackground (egg name), SlotBackground (the odds), AmountBackground (a 'Cost' label)
the odds band is FOUR preview slots, each one a pet preview plus a 'Chance' line plus a colour-coded 'Rarity' line — four is the readable count for an odds strip

hatch sequence, in order: egg tweens UP over 0.65s on Quad easing; oscillates left/right for TEN cycles with the delay starting at 0.11s and shrinking by 0.007s each cycle so the shake accelerates; snaps back to neutral; a flash ImageLabel grows and fades over 0.2s; camera blur steps down over ten steps as the pet appears; the hatch frame tweens DOWNWARD off-screen to dismiss
the revealed pet's name and rarity are held on screen briefly and then cleared as the blur finishes — the reveal has a hold, it does not cut

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/pet-simulator-x-open-egg/2205498 — fetched 2026-09-20; Scripting Support thread on reproducing Pet Simulator X's egg opening
demonstrates: the hatched pet in PSX is a real 3D model placed in world space in front of the camera, aligned to where its UI element sits — 'that's also how PSX do'

the stated reason is that ViewportFrame 'render[s] 3D model in a very bad quality and didn't rendering particle effects and graphic changes' — the reveal needs particles, so it cannot live inside the UI
the model is positioned by a camera-relative CFrame, not fixed world coordinates, because fixed positions that line up at 766x754 break at 1280x720
so the hatch screen is TWO layers: a UI layer holding the name, rarity and frame, and a world layer holding the pet — and the two are locked together by projection

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/ui-feedback-egg-hatching-system/673960 — fetched 2026-09-20; Creations Feedback thread on an egg-hatching game's pet panel
demonstrates: the detail panel is: pet art in a central box, pet name and stat labels, EQUIP and DELETE as the two bottom actions — equip and delete are a PAIR and they live at the bottom
progress readouts render as fraction bars ('0/3', '0/50') rather than percentages — a pet screen counts things, it does not measure them
a middle bar is reserved for modes such as multi-delete, i.e. bulk operations are a MODE strip between content and actions, not a button on every tile
critique: the name should sit ABOVE the image so the stats block below has room — art in the middle, identity above, numbers below

critique: saturated blue at full strength made reviewers 'want to keep looking away from it'; pure red text (255,0,0) with a (170,0,0) stroke read 'very bright and chunky'. Rarity colour has to be pulled off the primaries or the grid becomes unreadable at tile size
critique: setting the Rotation property made elements 'pixelated and cheap' — an angled badge or ribbon must be a pre-rotated image

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/easy-pet-system-plug-play-roblox-pet-system-hatch-equip-merge-multipliers/4535541 — fetched 2026-09-20; Community Resources listing for a shipped plug-and-play pet system
demonstrates: 'rarity colours are the source of truth. Set a rarity's colours once and every surface follows: the card in the Pets menu, the hatch toast, the egg billboard' — one rarity token, three surfaces, no per-screen colour decisions
the shipped ladder is five rarities: Common green, Uncommon blue, Rare purple, Epic red, Legendary yellow — twenty-eight pets spread across five tiers, roughly five or six pets per tier
hatching ships as single AND triple — the x1 / x3 pair is part of the egg panel, not an upsell bolted on
'Equip Best' and 'Merge All' are named, first-class buttons — the bulk action is a labelled button on the screen, not a hidden gesture

references.source: https://hopsdev.itch.io/essential-gui-pack — fetched 2026-09-20; a published Roblox GUI pack listing its twenty-plus screens
demonstrates: 'Pet Index' and 'Pet Inventory' are listed as SEPARATE GUIs — the collection book is not a tab of the bag, it is its own screen
'Egg Display' is a third, separate GUI, distinct from both — egg odds, held pets and the collection record are three screens, not one with filters

the surrounding pack (Achievements, Codes, Daily Rewards, Currencies Display, Rebirth, Sell Alert, Trading, Notifications) is one cartoon-styled family — a pet game's pet screens share their construction with its shop and reward screens rather than having a look of their own

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/what-is-the-best-pet-system-on-roblox-right-now/1822730 — fetched 2026-09-20; Scripting Support thread enumerating what a pet system is expected to contain
demonstrates: 'Pet Index' is named as an expected feature alongside hatching and equipping — the three-screen set is the genre's baseline, not a nice-to-have
the index is described as saving 'the pets you have already hatched', i.e. it is keyed on EVER-OBTAINED, so an entry stays filled after the pet is deleted or traded away
'Equip Best' is again named, with sorting by a configurable stat — the sort key is data, so the screen must render a sorted list it did not choose

references.source: https://v3nn7.itch.io/ultimate-pet-system-for-roblox-studio — fetched 2026-09-20; a published Roblox pet-system asset listing its UI
demonstrates: the DETAIL pane (one pet at a time) does get a live 3D preview, via a Module3D render inside the UI — the expensive renderer is affordable for one pet and not for a grid of them
a 'Unique Pet ID system (UID) — prevents duplicates' backs the inventory, so two visually identical tiles are distinct objects: selection, lock and delete must address a UID, not a pet name
the shipped screen set is again egg-opening, inventory, stats — the same three surfaces

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/placement-of-an-equipped-item-slot/3134434 — fetched 2026-09-20; Art Design Support thread on where an equipped slot belongs in an inventory screen
demonstrates: the recommendation is to 'have a separated section for the equipped item (like the slot for the left hand item) as well as potentially the player's character with the equipped item in a viewport'
equipped state is a PLACE on the screen, not only a badge drawn on a tile inside the grid

the answer is argued from the Minecraft convention — a distinct equipped area beside the grid, often next to a character preview — so it is a cross-genre expectation the pet strip inherits, not one game's idea
the asker's failing version was 'only a floating slot on the left side': one detached slot reads as debris, a labelled strip reads as capacity

rules.note: Distilled from the references above. Units are Roblox UI units: px for stroke and radius, seconds for timing, unitless for counts. This genre sits ON TOP of simulator.json — panel stroke, plaque header, overhanging red circular close, price pills and text stroke are inherited from there and are not repeated. What follows is only what a PET screen adds.

screenSet.rule: ship three separate screens, not one screen with filters: the bag (what is held now), the index (what has ever been obtained), and the egg panel (what can be obtained)
screenSet.never: a single Pets window with an Owned/All toggle
screenSet.why: the published GUI pack lists Pet Index, Pet Inventory and Egg Display as three separate GUIs, and the devforum enumeration of an expected pet system names index, inventory and hatching as three things

petTile.why: ViewportFrame 'do[es] not support particles' and lags 'if too many of them are used with models specially with a lot of parts'; the shipped look is a fixed-angle, fixed-light pre-render that 'looks much more like an image than a viewport frame'. The PS99-derived tile carried exactly image + level + rarity and no more.

detailPreview.rule: the one-pet detail pane MAY use a live 3D render; the grid may not
detailPreview.why: a shipped system pairs a Module3D preview in the detail pane with flat tiles in the grid — the cost is per visible model, so one is affordable and forty are not

grid.cellSizeRule: derive CellSize from the ScrollingFrame's inner width minus padding, then round DOWN to a whole number of columns
grid.why: the single loudest critique on the PS99-styled inventory was 'the content cant fully fit in the scrolling frame horizontally. adjust your cell size to make it fit!' — a fixed cell clips the right-hand column at the first resolution that is not the author's. Five columns rather than the shop grid's four because a pet bag holds hundreds of stacks where a shop holds a dozen offers.

rarityColour.rule: one colour per rarity, defined once, applied to the tile backing/stroke, the hatch reveal label and the egg odds line
rarityColour.never: a different rarity palette per screen, and never a fully saturated primary
rarityColour.why: 'rarity colours are the source of truth. Set a rarity's colours once and every surface follows: the card in the Pets menu, the hatch toast, the egg billboard.' The counter-example is the hatch panel whose pure (255,0,0) label read 'very bright and chunky' and whose full-strength blue made reviewers 'want to keep looking away from it' — at tile size a grid of full primaries is unreadable.

rarityLadder.pacing: roughly five to six pets per tier
rarityLadder.extendTo: up to nine tiers by appending above Legendary (Mythic, Secret), never by inserting below Common
rarityLadder.why: five is the ladder in both the shipped plug-and-play system (28 pets / 5 rarities) and in Adopt Me's classification (Common, Uncommon, Rare, Ultra-Rare, Legendary); larger games extend upward (Bubble Gum Simulator INFINITY runs nine with Secret at the top). Common is always the bottom and always the quiet colour.

rarityBorder.carrier: the tile's own stroke plus a tint on its backing
rarityBorder.never: a separate decorative frame image per rarity
rarityBorder.why: the rarity token has to survive being restated on the hatch reveal and the egg odds line, which have no tile to put a frame on; and the PS99-styled inventory failed review precisely because 'the UIStroke color is different between the X button and the frame' — one stroke system, recoloured per rarity, is the only version that stays coherent

variantAxis.rule: a variant (Gold / Rainbow / Shiny) is a SECOND mark on the tile, placed in a corner, and must not recolour the rarity backing
variantAxis.why: PS99 pets carry a rarity and independently a Golden 1.5x / Rainbow 3x / Shiny 5x variant; collapsing the two axes into one colour makes a Common Rainbow indistinguishable from a Legendary

stacking.rule: identical pets stack into one tile with an xN counter
stacking.why: a shipped system stacks duplicates with a counter and backs the bag with a 'Unique Pet ID system (UID) — prevents duplicates', so lock, delete and equip address an instance while the grid shows a stack

equipStrip.placement: a separate horizontal strip outside the grid
equipStrip.why: Bubble Gum Simulator INFINITY opens at four slots and caps at eleven from three different unlock sources, so the strip must render filled, empty and still-locked slots together; PS99 unlocks further slots by rank. The devforum recommendation for equipped items is 'a separated section for the equipped item ... as well as potentially the player's character with the equipped item' — equipped state is a place, not only a badge on a tile.

autoEquip.default: automatic — the top n pets by the sort stat are equipped without the player acting
autoEquip.why: PS99 equips the best eight by default and only offers manual selection behind an explicit 'Edit Mode' prompt; 'Equip Best' is named as a first-class button in two independent sources. A pet screen that opens in manual mode with empty slots is the wrong default for this genre.

toolbar.why: PS99's open pets menu carries exactly three icons across its top — a padlock, a pet face and a four-windows icon — and the pet-face icon is also the route back out of manual mode

bulkActions.rule: lock and mass-delete are MODES entered from a strip between the grid and the action row, not buttons repeated on every tile
bulkActions.why: the reviewed hatch/inventory panel reserved a middle bar for options such as multi-delete, and a shipped pet system exposes 'Merge All' as one labelled button; per-tile delete buttons on a grid of hundreds is the failure this avoids

detailPane.why: the reviewed panel put the name beside the art and was told to move it above so the stats had room; equip and delete sit together at the bottom as a pair

counters.rule: progress on a pet screen renders as a fraction (3/8, 0/50), not a percentage and not a bare number
counters.why: the reviewed panel used '0/3' and '0/50' bars; a pet game counts discrete things — slots, hatches, index entries — so the denominator is the information

eggPanel.anchoring: screen-space panel positioned by worldToScreenPoint on the egg and scaled by camera distance
eggPanel.neverAnchoring: a centred modal, or a raw BillboardGui
eggPanel.why: the hatch framework builds exactly NameBackground / SlotBackground / AmountBackground with four chance+rarity slots and tracks the egg by projection; single and triple hatch ship together in a published pet system

hatchReveal.renderer: a real 3D model positioned in front of the camera by a camera-relative CFrame
layers: world layer: the pet model and its particles
UI layer: name, rarity label, frame
sequence: shake: 10 left/right cycles, first delay 0.11s, each cycle 0.007s shorter, so the shake accelerates
flash: an ImageLabel grows and fades over 0.2s
blur steps down over 10 steps while the pet appears
dismiss: the frame tweens DOWNWARD off-screen
hatchReveal.why: the sequence and its numbers are the hatch framework's; the renderer choice is PSX's, whose stated reason is that ViewportFrame 'render[s] 3D model in a very bad quality and didn't rendering particle effects'. A reveal without particles is the tell that a generated pet game is fake, and a camera-relative CFrame is required because fixed world positions that line up at 766x754 break at 1280x720.

index.rule: an index entry stays filled after the pet is deleted, sold or traded away
index.why: the index is described as saving 'the pets you have already hatched' — keying it on current holdings would empty a player's collection every time they merge, and that is the single most common way this screen is built wrong
index.unownedTreatment: NOT OBSERVED — no fetched source described how an undiscovered entry is drawn, so the silhouette/question-mark convention is deliberately not asserted here

rotation.rule: never set the Rotation property on an angled badge, ribbon or label — ship a pre-rotated image
rotation.why: on the reviewed hatch UI, rotated elements read 'pixelated and cheap'. simulator.json's daily-reward banner sits at a deliberate angle, so this rule is how that angle gets built.

gapsAgainstShippedTheme: OPEN: the kit has no equip strip primitive at all — a horizontal strip that renders filled, empty and locked slots from a capacity number is the first missing piece.
OPEN: the kit's grid is the shop grid (4 across, from simulator.json). A pet bag needs 5 across with a cell size derived from the container, and derived cell sizing does not exist yet.
OPEN: no rarity token. Rarity colour has to be one value read by the tile, the hatch label and the egg odds line; today each surface would pick its own.
OPEN: no stack counter and no UID-addressed selection, so lock/delete would address a pet name and hit the wrong instance.
OPEN: the hatch reveal has no implementation. It is the only screen in this genre that needs a world-space model plus a projected UI layer, which is a capability the UI kit does not currently have.
OPEN: variant marking (Gold/Rainbow/Shiny) as a second corner mark is unbuilt; a generator would collapse it into the rarity colour.
NOT OBSERVED: how an undiscovered index entry is drawn. Five fetched sources describe the index existing; none describes its empty state.

renderedAndCompared.how: NOT YET DONE. These rules were distilled from fetched web sources on 2026-09-20 and have not been rendered in Studio and compared against anything. simulator.json's text-stroke defect was invisible in source and obvious on screen; until this genre goes through the same loop, every numeric value here is a reading, not a measurement.
